prompt: A city bike-share program wants to break even. The candidate's framework: (1) Rides per bike per day; (2) Revenue per ride; (3) Cost to buy and maintain each bike. What is the flaw in this framework?

options.text: Buckets 1 and 2 overlap: longer rides earn more per ride
options.feedback: Ride length affects revenue per ride, but how often bikes are used and what each ride earns are separate drivers.

options.text: Missing: the cost of stations and of moving bikes between them
options.feedback: Right. Docking stations and trucks that rebalance bikes are large costs that don't sit in any per-bike bucket. Without them, break-even looks closer than it is.

options.text: Bucket 3 doesn't belong: bikes are a one-time purchase
options.feedback: Bikes also need ongoing maintenance and replacement, so their cost belongs in a break-even view.

options.text: It's a generic profit tree: break-even needs a market-size view first
options.feedback: Revenue drivers against costs is the right start for break-even. The flaw is a missing cost line.

explanation: Break-even = rides × revenue per ride against bike costs plus system costs: stations, rebalancing trucks and staff. The system costs are missing.

extras.corrected_framework: Rides per bike; revenue per ride; bike purchase and maintenance; stations and rebalancing
